title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
disposition: Writ petition partly allowed (Commissioner's order set aside; appeal remitted to the pre-2003 forum)
headnote: An appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 — and its pre-deposit condition under Section 127(2) — lies only against a final order of assessment made under Section 126 of the 2003 Act. An assessment made under the pre-2003 regime (the U.P. Electricity Supply (Consumers) Regulations, 1984 or the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2002) is not a Section 126 order; Section 127 has no application to it, and no pre-deposit can be demanded. The right of appeal is a substantive vested right, governed by the law in force when the assessment proceedings were initiated, and is not divested by the 2003 Act, whose Section 185(2) & (5) (read with Section 6 of the General Clauses Act) preserve the earlier forum. The Commissioner therefore had no jurisdiction to reject the appeal under Section 127(2); it must be decided by the appellate forum under the earlier provisions.

holding_units.code: Electricity Act, 2003 (transition from U.P. Supply (Consumers) Regulations 1984 / U.P. Supply Code 2002)
holding_units.topic: Scope of the Section 127 appeal — confined to Section 126 orders; transitional assessments
holding_units.question: Does Section 127 of the 2003 Act (and its pre-deposit condition in s.127(2)) govern an appeal against an assessment made before the 2003 Act, under the U.P. Regulations 1984 / U.P. Supply Code 2002?
holding_units.holding: No. Section 127(1) confines the appeal to a final order 'made under Section 126' of the 2003 Act; a pre-2003 assessment is not such an order, so neither Section 127 nor its pre-deposit condition applies. Section 185(2) & (5) (with Section 6 of the General Clauses Act) preserve the pre-2003 assessment and its appellate forum. The Commissioner's rejection under s.127(2) was without jurisdiction; the appeal is remitted to the forum under Regulations 1984 / Code 2002.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Assessments for excess load were made on 3.4.2002 (under Regulations 1984) and 13.12.2002 (under Code 2002); the appeal was filed in 2003 before the appellate committee (which required no pre-deposit) and only later transmitted to the Commissioner, who demanded a one-third pre-deposit under s.127(2).
holding_units.flag: Multi-regime transitional case: it construes the pre-2005 U.P. regime (Regulations 1984 and U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2002), not the 2005 Code.

principle_tags.application: The right of appeal is a substantive right that vests when the original (here, assessment) proceedings are initiated, governed by the law then in force, and is not taken away by a later statute unless expressly or by necessary intendment; a new pre-deposit condition cannot be imposed on such a vested appeal.

lead_authorities.name: Garikapati Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhry
Shiv Shakti Coop. Housing Society v. Swaraj Developers

principle_tags.application: A change of forum is not a matter of pure procedure; once proceedings are validly initiated before a forum, that vested right continues despite a later change of jurisdiction, unless the legislature clearly provides otherwise.

not_decided.point: Consequences of the appellate committee's long inaction
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to go into the effect/consequence of the appeal remaining pending with the appellate committee from 2003 to 2008; it proceeded straight to the jurisdiction question.

authorities.name: Colonial Sugar Refining Co. Ltd. v. Irving
authorities.proposition: The right of appeal is a substantive right that vests on the initiation of proceedings; only procedural statutes may be retrospective, not those affecting the right of appeal.
authorities.how_treated: Referred as the foundational statement of the principle.

authorities.name: Nana bin Aba v. Skeku bin Andu
authorities.proposition: Followed Colonial Sugar Refining on the vested, substantive nature of the right of appeal.
authorities.how_treated: Referred within the line of authority.

authorities.name: Delhi Cloth & General Mills Co. Ltd. v. Income Tax Commissioner, Delhi
authorities.proposition: Only a statute dealing with procedure may have retrospective effect; a statute conferring substantive rights, including the right of appeal, does not.
authorities.how_treated: Referred within the line of authority.

authorities.name: Indira Sohanlal v. Custodian of Evacuee Property, Delhi
authorities.proposition: Observed that the right of appeal in a pending action may be a substantive vesting right, but left the question open.
authorities.how_treated: Referred; the open question was later settled in Garikapati.

authorities.name: Garikapati Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhry
authorities.proposition: Leading five-principle statement: the right of appeal is a vested substantive right governed by the law at the institution of the suit/proceeding, preserved through all appellate stages, and can be taken away only by express enactment or necessary intendment.

authorities.name: Kirpa Singh v. Ajaypal Singh
authorities.proposition: Right of appeal governed by law at the date of institution of the suit, not at the date of decision or of filing the appeal.

authorities.name: Manujendra Dutt v. Purnedu Prosad Roy Chowdhury
authorities.proposition: Deletion of a provision (there, s.29 of the Calcutta Thika Tenancy Act) does not divest the forum of jurisdiction over proceedings validly transferred and pending before it, absent a contrary provision.

authorities.name: Maria Cristina De Souza Sodder v. Amria Zurana Pereira Pinto
authorities.proposition: The right of appeal is a substantive right that vests when the lis commences and is not affected by a repeal unless the repealing enactment expressly or by necessary implication takes it away.

authorities.name: Ramesh Singh v. Cinta Devi
authorities.proposition: A vested right of appeal under the old Motor Vehicles Act is not dislodged by the new Act; the appellant may appeal without the pre-deposit required by the proviso to s.173 of the new Act.
authorities.how_treated: Followed as the most apt authority.

authorities.name: Hoosein Kasam Dada (India) Ltd. v. State of M.P.
authorities.proposition: Unless the new Act expressly or by necessary implication is retrospective, the right of appeal crystallises on institution and a new deposit condition cannot be imposed.

authorities.name: State of Bombay v. Supreme General Films Exchange Ltd.
authorities.proposition: To the same effect on the vested right of appeal.

authorities.name: Vitthalbhai Narangbhai Patel v. CST
authorities.proposition: To the same effect on the vested right of appeal.

authorities.name: CIT, Bangalore v. R. Sharadamma
authorities.proposition: Where an authority is validly seized of a matter on a reference, it does not lose jurisdiction on a later amendment; change of forum is not mere procedure but a vested right.

authorities.name: CIT v. Dhadi Sahu
authorities.proposition: A law changing the forum does not affect pending actions unless a contrary intention is clearly shown; the forum of appeal is a vested right, not pure procedure.

authorities.name: Shiv Shakti Coop. Housing Society, Nagpur v. Swaraj Developers
authorities.proposition: An appeal is a continuation of the original proceedings; the right of appeal is statutory and, once conferred, a vested substantive right, distinct from the inherent right to sue.
